evals.prompt: write an ansible playbook to ensure nginx is installed and running
evals.expected_output: Uses the apt/package and service modules to declare desired state rather than raw shell commands, so reported changed/ok status is honest and a second run against the same host reports zero changes.

evals.prompt: running our playbook twice still shows changes the second time
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses tasks using raw shell/command instead of idempotent modules (or shell commands missing creates/changed_when guards), and treats any 'changed' on an already-configured host as a bug to fix so reruns converge to zero changes.

evals.prompt: our fleet autoscales and gets replaced constantly, let's still write a big convergence playbook for it
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: config management solves drift reconciliation on long-lived mutable hosts, but for an autoscaled, frequently-replaced fleet, baking a golden image and replacing instances (immutable-infrastructure) is simpler and more reliable, and the choice should be a documented decision.
